decisions.reason: As a core drainage component using the firm's existing drainage engineering and system-integration knowledge, it fits high absorptive capacity and its dedicated visibility in 2018-2019 suggests enough traction to continue refining rather than withdraw.

A floor-level shower drainage system is directly in the firm's strategic direction and core knowledge base, and its stronger standalone presentation by 2019 indicates the firm can learn from the launch and build it further.

The product is close to the firm's design-oriented shower drainage expertise, but the reduced prominence after launch suggests more uncertain demand, so management would likely keep it as a differentiated niche unless performance weakens further.

An integrated-slope shower element complements the firm's established installation and waterproofing know-how and strengthens the product family, making it more likely to be retained even if marketed mainly as part of a system.

This backflow-protected basement drain extends the firm's proven drainage and safety capabilities into a closely related application, and the strong launch messaging and homepage visibility point to a product worth keeping.

An air-admittance valve is more peripheral to the firm's main shower and floor-drainage competence, and with only limited website prominence the firm is less likely to see enough learning advantage or strategic fit to keep it.
